text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Extensive coverage by foreign media of local council elections.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali meets James Baker, United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara, in London over ways to break deadlock over referendum.
- Elections mark decisive step towards reinforcement of local democracy.
- Five foreign holdings qualify in preliminary selection for the tender due in September to build a $300 million port in Tangier.
- Gang arrested in southern city of Agadir, charged with stealing and selling luxury cars with fake licence plates.
- Despite commitments of all parties to ensure fairness of polls, irregularities tarnished local council elections.
- James Baker to convene two-day meeting in Portugal on June 23, between Morocco, the Polisario Front, Algeria and Mauritania, over Western Sahara issue.
